newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Oct 9.

text.p: The following is a summary of major Indonesian political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Jakarta. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.
President Suharto said social inequality can happen anywhere but Indonesia should make sure it is not manipulated by subversive forces in society.

The Indonesian Embassy in the Netherlands said on Tuesday that it would complain to The Hague over accusations made in a Dutch newspaper that one of their staff is involved in an Ecstasy smuggling ring. The embassy said there are no grounds for the charges and that, up until now, they have not been contacted by Dutch authorities.
Trials of 64 people arrested in connection with the July 27 riots in Jakarta open on Wednesday at the Jakarta Central Court.
Areas of south Jakarta have flooded due to heavy rain over the past two days, reaching levels around 200 cm.

Indonesia was likely to end-up in trade wars with its major trading partners Japan, the United States and the European Union if Indonesia insisted on carrying out its national car policy, a noted economist said. The Timor national car has been given preferential tax and tariff treatment by the Indonesian government.
